summary: Verified independently as a pure move. `git show :sequencer/src/main/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitLog.java | tail -n +3` is byte-identical to `git show HEAD:ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/CommitLog.java | tail -n +3`, and the same holds for the test -- the package line is the only content change in either file. No request-rate change is possible from a byte-identical move; `committingCostsExactlyOneRequestWhenUncontended` still pins puts()==1, so the one cost assertion in the file travelled with it. `GATE_SCOPE=full ./scripts/check-module.sh` re-run green (8 modules, rule5 tested 4, rule2 tested 2). architecture.md's dependency rule 2 names only `plugin` as forbidden from `binstore-backends`; sequencer's new testImplementation line matches ingest's precedent verbatim and its comment is true (CommitLogTest:182-188 really does count requests through CountingBinStore over a real MemoryBinStore). Both READMEs already described the post-move split (sequencer/README.md:3 'the write-once commit log'; ingest/README.md lists no commit log), so no doc update was owed. All 9 tests re-recorded in .harness/tdd/red.json under binjava.sequencer.CommitLogTest#* with the moved file's sha256 -- re-recording against real mutations was the right call over SKIP=check-tdd, because a skip would have left nine tests in a new module with no falsifiability evidence at all. Suite re-run by me from a clean tree: 432 total, 0 failures, ingest 84, sequencer 26 -- the row's numbers hold exactly. The CommitLog javadoc's M1-era notes ('commit log v0 (M1.10)', 'slot 0 / epoch 0 in M1 ... so that M4's leases and epochs are not a key-grammar change') are dated historical statements that are still true and are, if anything, more apt now that the file sits in the module that will own leases and epochs; nothing there is stale, and rewriting it here would have destroyed the purity that is this task's entire reason for existing. Three minor findings, none blocking.

findings.title: A seventh reference to CommitLog was missed: the {@link} now dangles
findings.description:
The row enumerates six updated call sites and presents that list as complete. There is a seventh reference: IntervalPutRateTest's class javadoc says `

⚠️ ONLY {@link SegmentPublisher}, no {@link CommitLog}: ...`. That file is in package binjava.ingest and imports no CommitLog, so after the move the symbol is unresolvable from its compilation unit. It is javadoc-only, so javac with -Xlint:all -Werror does not see it (doclint is not enabled in binjava.java-conventions.gradle.kts) and no gate catches it -- which is exactly why it survived. The reference is load-bearing prose, not decoration: it is the sentence that explains why this test measures SegmentPublisher's PUTs alone and excludes the commit-log append from ADR-0016's PUT/s table.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone running ./gradlew javadoc, or an IDE resolving the link, gets 'reference not found' for {@link CommitLog}, and a reader following the cross-reference that justifies the test's cost boundary lands nowhere. Fix is one line: qualify it as {@link binjava.sequencer.CommitLog}.

findings.title: The rewritten import is left in the old slot, breaking alphabetical order in all three files where an import was rewritten rather than added
findings.description: The three files that GAINED an import (DefaultIngest, DefaultIngestTest, SubscriptionHubTest) place binjava.sequencer.CommitLog correctly, after binjava.security.Principal and before java.io. The three where an import was REWRITTEN in place leave it where binjava.ingest.CommitLog used to sort: SearchableIT.java:15 sits between binjava.ingest.Accumulator and binjava.ingest.IngestConfig; ShardFanOutIT.java:14 sits before binjava.ingest.SubscriptionHub; EndToEndTest.java:16 sits between binjava.ingest.Accumulator and binjava.ingest.IngestConfig. Every other import in all three files is in strict ASCII order, so this is the only exception in each. No formatter or import-order gate exists in .pre-commit-config.yaml, so nothing will catch it.
findings.failure_scenario: The next person adding a binjava.ingest or binjava.sequencer import to one of these files either sorts correctly and produces a diff that looks like it moved an unrelated line, or copies the local anomaly and spreads it. If an import-order formatter is ever adopted, these three files churn for reasons unrelated to whatever commit adopts it.

findings.title: The claim 'Every mutation was reverted and the tree verified clean' was not true throughout the review window -- I observed the apply(delta) mutation live in the working tree
findings.description: The last red record for these tests was written at 08:16-08:17 (.harness/tdd/red.json, at=1788387363..1788387437). At 08:19, git status reported `RM sequencer/src/main/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitLog.java` and `git diff` on that path showed exactly the mutation the row names first: `-                apply(delta);` removed from the putIfAbsent success branch. sequencer/build/test-results/test/TEST-binjava.sequencer.CommitLogTest.xml was rewritten at 08:20:53 with tests=9 failures=5, so a suite run happened against the mutated source AFTER the red records were complete. By 08:21 the tree had settled clean and has stayed clean; I then ran ./gradlew test --rerun-tasks myself from that clean tree and got 432/0 failures with ingest 84 and sequencer 26. So the staged bytes are correct and the row's numbers are correct -- I verified both independently -- but the specific sentence 'Every mutation was reverted and the tree verified clean' describes a state that did not hold continuously, and non-negotiable 4 is about claims, not outcomes. Several concurrent sessions are running in this checkout, so I cannot attribute the window, only report it.
findings.failure_scenario: The mutation in question is silent and severe: dropping apply(delta) means nextOffsets never advances on a successful commit, so every subsequent segment restarts each stream's offsets at the same value -- a direct I2 violation ('a committed offset is never reassigned') that a consumer sees as an infinite replay. git commit would have committed the clean index regardless, and pre-commit stashes unstaged work, so this commit is safe; the exposure is the NEXT commit in this checkout silently carrying it. Concrete action before committing: confirm `git diff` prints nothing, not merely that `git diff --cached` looks right.
